name: The AI Enablement Audit
title: The AI Enablement Audit
answer: The AI enablement audit is a structured review of how an organization can safely adopt or expand AI systems. It maps existing and planned AI uses, the data and models involved, and the business processes they touch. The audit distinguishes between internal productivity tools, customer-facing applications, and third-party AI services. Its output is a prioritized inventory of enablement opportunities and control gaps, not a pass or fail verdict.

sections.body: The AI enablement audit is a structured review of how an organization can safely adopt or expand AI systems. It maps existing and planned AI uses, the data and models involved, and the business processes they touch. The audit distinguishes between internal productivity tools, customer-facing applications, and third-party AI services. Its output is a prioritized inventory of enablement opportunities and control gaps, not a pass or fail verdict.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The audit runs on the organization's existing governance, security, and IT asset records. It typically uses document review, configuration extracts from cloud and identity systems, and interviews with system owners. Where model inventories or AI registries exist, the audit reads from those; where they do not, it builds a lightweight register from procurement and engineering records. No dedicated machine learning infrastructure is required to perform the audit itself.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done in three passes. First, the auditor identifies AI systems through procurement logs, code repositories, and user surveys. Second, each system is classified by data sensitivity, decision impact, and degree of human oversight. Third, controls are tested against a recognized framework, such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and findings are tied to specific enablement actions. The method is deliberately vendor-neutral and repeatable across business units.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk and provenance are treated as a single control area. The audit checks whether training data and model provenance are documented, whether third-party terms permit the intended use, and whether intellectual property and privacy obligations are mapped to each system. It also reviews incident response, access controls, and the ability to trace a model output back to its version and data. Because the field sits within The AI Lawyer, the audit pays close attention to active litigation patterns and regulatory filings as early indicators of control failures.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The audit is moving from a one-time project to a continuous function. As AI systems become embedded in procurement, HR, and customer operations, the audit will increasingly run against live system telemetry and model registries rather than static documents. Expect the scope to expand into agentic workflows, where a model acts across multiple tools, and into contractual AI clauses that shift liability between vendor and customer. The practice is likely to converge with existing third-party risk and privacy audit cycles.
